Who Selected Which Choice

Source: R/analysis_pipeline.R
ck_sm_selection_matrix.Rd

The single place that decides whether a select_multiple cell counts as a selection, so "selected" can never mean two things in one run. Two export styles are detected per column:

Usage

ck_sm_selection_matrix(
  dataset,
  parent,
  sm_separator = "/",
  sm_child_style = c("auto", "label", "dummy"),
  exclude_choices = NULL,
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset

A dataframe.

parent

The select_multiple parent variable name.

sm_separator

Separator between parent and choice. Default "/".

sm_child_style

"auto" (default), "label" or "dummy".

exclude_choices

Optional choice labels to leave out entirely.

ignore_case

Logical. Match exclude_choices case-insensitively.

Value

NULL if the parent has no children, otherwise a list with selected (logical matrix), columns, suffixes and styles.

Details

"label"

MMC 4Mi ONA style - the cell holds the choice label when selected and is blank otherwise, so any non-blank value is a selection. This is the only safe rule for these exports: real choice labels include "None", "No" and "Refused", and treating those strings as negatives would zero out genuine answers.

"dummy"

The cell holds 0/1 or TRUE/FALSE, so only 1 / TRUE is a selection.

Detection is conservative: a column is a dummy only when every non-blank value in it is one of 0, 1, TRUE, FALSE. No masking is applied.
